topics: Basic Concepts and Fundamentals: Fluid statics
Description of fluid motion –Types of motion of fluid elements
Vorticity and circulation– Concept of rotational and irrotational flows
Equation of motion of forced and free vortex flow
Stream function and its relation with velocity field
`1 – Relation between stream function and velocity potential for a 2-D irrotational and incompressible flow
Pipe Flow: Viscous flow: Reynolds experiment to classify laminar and turbulent flows
shear stress and velocity distribution in a pipe
real life problems causing water hammer
Concept of Boundary Layer : Growth of boundary layer over a flat plate and definition of boundary layer thickness
Von- Karman momentum integral equations for the boundary layers
separation of boundary and methods of control
Dimensional  Analysis and Hydraulic similitude: Dimensional  analysis
important dimensional numbers and their significance
Froude, Reynold, Weber, Cauchy and Mach laws- Applications and limitations of model testing

partA.description: 2 Questions from each module. Total of 8 Questions, each carrying 3 marks

partB.description: Each question carries 9 marks. Two questions will be given from each module, out of which 1 question should be answered. Each question can have a maximum of 3 sub divisions.

courseOutcomes.description: Describe the concept of potential flow theory
Demonstrate the concept of viscosity on flow characteristics in diverse fluid flow problems
Use dimensional analysis to design physical or numerical experiments and to apply dynamic similarity
